question.text: Which statutory/regulatory framework governs the registration and conduct of a 'Registered Valuer' typically appointed by an AIF for valuation of unlisted securities?

answer.text: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) under the Companies Act 2013 / Registered Valuers framework, combined with professional membership (ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI/CFA)
ICAI alone, under a Chartered Accountants Act notification
RBI under the Banking Regulation Act

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 14.14, the independent valuer must be registered with IBBI (Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India) under the Registered Valuers framework flowing from Section 247 of the Companies Act 2013, AND hold professional membership of ICAI / ICSI / ICMAI / CFA Institute. SEBI's role is to add AIF-specific eligibility on top. The Trap: Option A misses IBBI. Option C understates multi-institution oversight. Option D is the wrong regulator. Cross-Exam Context: III-A (Compliance) touches on the Companies Act valuer framework. XIX-C merges IBBI-registration with SEBI's AIF-specific 3-year-experience and non-associate criteria. Manager's Pro-Tip: When shortlisting valuers, ask for BOTH the IBBI registration certificate AND the SEBI Circular Sept-2024 fit-test self-certification. Some IBBI-registered valuers are NOT SEBI-AIF-eligible due to associate-relationship with your sponsor.
